VLOOKUP Text-Number Mismatch Fix
VLOOKUP fails with #N/A when the lookup value is text but the source table has numbers due to data type mismatch; fix it by either converting the lookup value to a number in the formula or standardizing the source table formats.

Excel Data Setup Context
This guide assumes the lookup value (e.g., in cell A2) appears as a number but is text (green triangle indicator), while the source table's first column (e.g., B:B in another sheet) holds true numbers. Exact ranges like =VLOOKUP(A2, Sheet2!B:C, 2, FALSE) are used in examples.

Formula-Based Fixes
Use these modified VLOOKUP formulas to handle the text lookup value without changing source data:

Text to Number Conversion (Primary Fix):
=VLOOKUP(VALUE(A2), Sheet2!B:C, 2, FALSE)
The VALUE function converts text "4399" to number 4399 for matching.[1][3]

Quick Arithmetic Trick:
=VLOOKUP(A2+0, Sheet2!B:C, 2, FALSE)
Adding zero forces text-to-number conversion inline.[1]

Number to Text Conversion (If Source is Text, Reverse Scenario):
=VLOOKUP(TEXT(A2, "0"), Sheet2!B:C, 2, FALSE)
TEXT ensures number lookup matches text source.[3]

Test Data Types First:
=ISTEXT(A2) returns TRUE if lookup is text; =ISNUMBER(B9) checks source cell.[2]

Formatting-Based Fixes
Standardize source table or lookup column permanently:

Convert Source Text to Numbers (If Needed):
1. Select source column (e.g., Sheet2!B:B).
2. Click green error triangle > Convert to Number.
Or use Paste Special: Copy empty cell, select range, right-click > Paste Special > Add.[1][4][5]

Convert Lookup Text to Numbers:
1. Select lookup cells (e.g., A:A).
2. Data tab > Text to Columns > Finish (triggers conversion).
Or multiply by 1: Enter 1 in helper cell, copy, Paste Special > Multiply.[5]

Verify Post-Fix:
Recalculate with F9; green triangles disappear for true numbers.[4]

VLOOKUP Troubleshooting Table

| Issue Indicator | Test Formula | Formula Fix | Formatting Fix |
|-----------------|--------------|-------------|----------------|
| Green triangle on lookup | =ISTEXT(A2) | =VLOOKUP(VALUE(A2), table, col, FALSE) | Text to Columns > Finish |
| #N/A despite visual match | =ISNUMBER(B9) | =VLOOKUP(A2+0, table, col, FALSE) | Error icon > Convert to Number |
| Extra spaces suspected | =LEN(TRIM(A2)) vs =LEN(A2) | =VLOOKUP(TRIM(VALUE(A2)), table, col, FALSE) | =TRIM in helper column [4] |
